title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Grothendieck proved a gluing theorem. If Y -> X is a mono in a presheaf category Â and the square Y->X, Y->Y', Y'->X' is cocartesian, then applying A_/(-) gives a square in (Cat) that is both cartesian and cocartesian. Its horizontal arrows are fibrant monos, hence open immersions. Corollary: if Y->X (resp. Y->Y') is in W, then Y'->X' (resp. X->X') is in W. In modern terms, pushouts in Cat coming from presheaf monos via the slice construction are homotopy pushouts.

This page ('Mais attention') warns that the naive generalisation to arbitrary cocartesian squares in (Cat) is false. Take a pushout square Y -i-> X, g: Y->Y', f: X->X', i': Y'->X' with i a closed (or open) immersion, i.e. a fully faithful sieve or cosieve inclusion. It is NOT true in general that g in W implies f in W, nor that i in W implies i' in W. In particular it fails when Y' = e is the final category.

Counterexample. Let Z be a small category.
- Č(Z) is the cone on Z: Z with a cone point e_{w0} adjoined.
- Gluing two cones along Z gives the suspension ΣZ: Z plus two cone points, w0 mapping into Z and Z mapping to the other point. This is the pushout of Č(Z) <- Z -> Č(Z), and both inclusions are immersions.
- Set Y = Č(Z) ⊂ X = ΣZ. Then g: Y -> e is in W, since a cone has a final or initial object and is aspherical.
- Form the pushout X' = Θ(Y), obtained by collapsing Č(Z) to a point inside ΣZ.

Computing the pushout in Cat: X' has two objects, e_{w0'} and the collapsed point. Each arrow w0 -> z becomes an arrow to the point, and these are identified along the arrows of Z. Hence Hom(e_{w0'}, e_{y0'}) ≅ π_0(Z), and X' is the 'Kronecker' category with |π_0(Z)| parallel arrows. Its nerve is a wedge of |π_0(Z)|-1 circles, so X' ≃ Δ^1 (aspherical) iff Z is 0-connected. In that case f is in W iff ΣZ is W-aspherical. This fails e.g. for Z connected with non-trivial homology, such as nontrivial abelianised π_1. So f ∉ W although g ∈ W and i is an immersion: pushout along a sieve or cosieve is not a homotopy pushout in Cat.

Purpose. The example shows that the fibrancy hypothesis of the previous page's theorem is essential. It also sets up the next page's calculus of fractions for W_A in Â, where such gluing does work.
errors: The sufficient condition at the end, read as 'π_1 ≠ 1', is not quite right. For connected Z, ΣZ is simply connected, so ΣZ is contractible iff Z is acyclic (H̃_*(Z;Z)=0). There exist connected Z with nontrivial (perfect) π_1 that are acyclic, for which ΣZ is contractible and f IS a weak equivalence. The correct condition is H̃_*(Z) ≠ 0, e.g. π_1^ab ≠ 0. This may simply be a transcription or reading issue.
The marginal claim 'il semblerait évident' (some connectivity condition on g) is illegible, so it cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Pushouts in Cat along fully faithful sieve/cosieve inclusions (immersions) are not homotopy pushouts; weak equivalences are not stable under such cobase change.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of left properness / homotopy-pushout property for general sieves; need for Dwyer maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1980, Dwyer maps and the Thomason model structure); Cisinski (Astérisque 308)
ideas.where_published: Related discussions of immersions and asphericity appear in Pursuing Stacks; this exact example is unsure

ideas.what: Explicit computation: collapsing a cone Č(Z) inside the suspension ΣZ gives a two-object category with Hom ≅ π_0(Z).
ideas.modern_name: Pushout computation in Cat; Kronecker quiver category; nerve ≃ wedge of circles

ideas.what: Contrast with the previous page: pushouts of fibrant open immersions coming from presheaf monos are homotopy cocartesian.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushouts along (co)fibrations / Grothendieck fibrations that are sieves

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct (modulo the π_1 remark) counterexample showing sieve pushouts are not homotopy pushouts in Cat. That phenomenon is well known since Thomason's introduction of Dwyer maps. The explicit Hom ≅ π_0(Z) computation is a nice detail but routine.
transcription_corrections: 'Σ'(Z)' is the suspension ΣZ (two cones glued along Z); the later line correctly reads 'ΣZ est W-asph'.
'Θ(Y)' denotes the pushout X' obtained by collapsing Y = Č(Z) to a point.
Top right likely reads: 'si i ∈ W, a-t-on i' ∈ W ? ... (Ex Y, X asphériques, Y' = e) Non'.
Last line likely: 'prendre p.ex. Z à π_0 réduit à un point, ... π_1 ≠ 1' (i.e. Z connected, non-simply-connected).
